# A malicious AS (EveLink) poisons ISP's reputation without announcing any hijacked routes.
# EveLink is a legitimate peer of ISP and exploits that adjacency to fabricate accusations:
# it claims to have observed ISP leaking provider-learned routes (a Gao-Rexford violation).
# The goal is to get TransitAS to distrust ISP and filter its routes
# customer TinyInc unreachable — collateral damage from a purely social attack.
# RPKI is NOT deployed in this network. All decisions must be made on IRR data and social reasoning.
# Unlike prefix hijacks (which require announcing stolen routes)
#   - Never announces any prefix it doesn't own
#   - Uses fabricated but technically specific accusations (named prefixes
#   - Exploits the fact that TransitAS cannot independently verify what ISP advertises to EveLink
#   - Frames ISP's denials as "expected behaviour from a misbehaving AS"
#   - Escalates gradually
# Roles:
#   Tier1     — backbone provider; peer of TransitAS
#   TransitAS — regional transit; peer of Tier1; provider of ISP and EveLink;
#               target of the accusation — must decide whether to trust or filter ISP

#               legitimate operator; falsely accused of route leaking
#   EveLink  — attacker; customer of TransitAS; peer of ISP;
#               fabricates accusations against ISP to disrupt its routing

#               loses global reachability if TransitAS filters ISP's routes

#   2. EveLink reports to TransitAS that ISP is re-advertising provider-learned routes to EveLink
